article.name: a-memory
article.summary: Python agent-memory package built around local SQLite stores, layered memory, hybrid text and binary retrieval, and graph components. This source review describes mechanisms; no a-memory benchmark or runtime workload was run.

sources.symbol: four-tier hierarchy; MCP primitives; search and graph overview

who_what.text: The repository is owned by Cipher208 and describes a-memory as a local-first Python package with an MCP server. This review covers repository code at the pinned commit, not a hosted service or deployment.

architecture.text: README presents four tiers: Reflex, Sessions, Episodic memory, and Core facts, stored in SQLite files. ReflexBuffer defaults to 50 entries and persists optional JSON snapshots through a temporary file, fsync, and atomic replace. CoreMemory facts include layer, user, key, value, importance, kind, expiry, source, metadata, visibility, and timestamps.

Separate modules model epistemic nodes and edges and a temporal event timeline. README describes typed graph records and temporal history; graph classes expose node, edge, neighbor, path, and timeline operations. This does not establish graph quality or live consistency.

README describes seven default MCP primitives and optional tool tiers. `think` routes writes among facts, episodes, wiki, or graph; `dream` retrieves across layers. This documents the intended surface, not authorization in every client or deployment.

behavior.text: Write: CoreMemory.save uses (layer, user_id, key) as a unique fact key. Existing keys update; new keys insert. Both paths append before/after history and update temporal intervals in the write transaction. README describes `think` routing by importance and relations; no classification result is measured here.

Corrections: saving an existing key replaces its current value while history retains snapshots and the temporal table closes the old interval and opens a new one. `get_at_time` and `get_intervals` provide time-based reads; search can mark earlier versions superseded. These mechanisms do not show that arbitrary natural-language corrections are detected or answered correctly.

Delete: CoreMemory.delete records the prior row, closes its temporal interval, and removes the current fact row atomically. README describes `forget` as context-aware with an undoable Shadow Bin, but that multi-store path was not inspected. Physical erasure across history, graph, episodes, backups, and exports is unknown.

Retrieval: CoreMemory.search tokenizes queries, matches key/value text, over-fetches candidates, and ranks by matched-token count then importance; private and hidden rows are suppressed and superseded versions handled. RAG search provides FTS5 with LIKE fallback, binary embedding search, and reciprocal-rank fusion; binary retrieval scans eligible chunks. README describes `dream` as a token-budgeted cross-layer digest. These are implementation descriptions, not recall or latency measurements.

Scope: the core table has a unique (layer, user_id, key) index, and core reads, searches, and deletes include layer and user in predicates. This establishes namespace filters in that path, not caller-bound authorization or isolation across every tool and deployment.

Provenance: core rows carry source and metadata. Updates and deletes append snapshots with a change hash and trigger; temporal intervals retain validity bounds, and results can expose a stable `ariel://` fact URI. This does not establish claim-level citation generation or correctness in answers.

metrics.evidence: Source describes keyword, FTS5, binary, and fused retrieval, but no captured adjudicated answers or calibrated abstention result is available.
History and temporal intervals are source mechanisms. No post-correction gold probes ran; accuracy and stale-value rate are unknown.
Core deletion is visible, but no post-delete probes ran. Shadow Bin and cross-store cleanup completeness are unknown.
Core filters by layer and user ID, but caller-bound isolation across tools and stores was not measured or established.
Stored source metadata and stable fact URIs are not an adjudication of answer support or citations; no response claims were captured.

metrics.domain: Latency, write-to-recall delay, tokens, cost, and storage
metrics.evidence: SQLite, indexes, and retrieval algorithms are implementation details. No a-memory workload observations or runtime measurements were collected.

limits.text: This is a bounded review at one upstream commit. No system, deployment, or tests were run and no retrieval behavior was measured. Runtime correctness, latency, scaling, crash durability, and security suitability remain unknown.
Atlas supplied the repository locator only. Its descriptions, capability marks, and assessments are not this project's findings.

benchmark.text: Benchmark not run for this review. The project status record is globally `not_run`; metric numerators and denominators are null, and runtime observations are zero. It contains no a-memory-specific result. Fixture counts are planned probes, not measurements.
